crop.notes: Clipping holds only the Allen/Mrs. Duffy section of the longer story 'Drunken Brawl Ends Fatally'; the headline and opening paragraphs on Brown's death are left out. The Allen passage itself is complete.

ocr.notes: Gist readable but a vertical fold line garbles many words (e.g. 'whole thing', 'new turn', 'seized', 'strike').

title.suggested: Tom Allen helps police solve fatal saloon assault

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen told police his housekeeper, Mrs. Mary Duffy, saw from a window over his saloon the assault on William C. Brown at the Ohio saloon opposite, leading to bartender William Damm's arrest for murder.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Friday Morning, July 16, 1897, page 12.

facts.fact: Allen informed police that his housekeeper, Mrs. Mary Duffy, had witnessed the fatal assault on William C. Brown at the Ohio saloon across the street from Allen's saloon; Allen and Duffy were summoned before Chief Desmond and bartender William Damm was charged with first-degree murder
places: Tom Allen's saloon, opposite the Ohio saloon, St. Louis

notes: Mrs. Mary Duffy is named as Allen's housekeeper and sat at a window over his saloon.
